page: Amazon Web Services x8g.48xlarge is a high-density, memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by AWS Graviton generation 8 architecture, the instance incorporates 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs based on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V2 design running at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz. The system provides single-threaded execution per core without simultaneous multithreading, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory provisioning reaches 3072 GB of system RAM, yielding an extensive 16 GB per core allocation.

Hardware connectivity includes a baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps managed by Nitro controllers, while local NVMe storage is omitted entirely, necessitating external EBS network volumes for persistent block storage. The platform contains no hardware accelerators or discrete GPUs. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via native ARM AES instructions, though x86-specific vector extensions are naturally absent.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded scaling and memory throughput. The instance recorded 314,681.65 on multi-core stress-ng tests and reached 895.67 GB/sec uncached large-block read bandwidth, placing both metrics in the top tier. Database and in-memory operations are equally elevated, achieving 359.81 million operations per second in Redis SET throughput and top-tier PassMark database scores. Conversely, per-core metrics such as single-threaded Geekbench (1,643) and stress-ng (1,644.19) reflect average mid-range performance, indicating that application scale depends on parallel thread distribution rather than isolated single-core frequency.

The x8g.48xlarge presents high qualitative cost efficiency for organizations that can fully saturate its massive memory space and parallel ARM threads. Tradeoffs center on the absence of bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures, and modest single-core throughput. It is ideally configured for large-scale in-memory key-value stores such as Redis or Memcached, in-memory relational databases, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise ETL pipelines that require massive memory density.
description: Amazon Web Services x8g.48xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server driven by 192 dedicated AWS Neoverse-V2 arm64 physical cores operating at 2.7 GHz. Governed by the Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides 3072 GB of system RAM, creating a large 16 GB per core ratio designed for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs, relying on a 50 Gbps baseline network fabric for cluster communication and external block storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth, evidenced by 314,681.65 on stress-ng multi-core and 359.81 million Redis SET operations per second, contrasted with average single-core throughput. The architecture delivers strong resource density and efficiency for parallel workloads, making it well suited for large in-memory caching layers, massive distributed databases, and high-throughput memory-resident data pipelines.
